analysis: The method mapEntry creates a singleton map from the provided key and value using `Collections.singletonMap(key, value)`. This map contains exactly one entry. Then it obtains the entry set, which is a `Set` with exactly one element, and gets an iterator over that set. Calling `next()` on this iterator will always return the single entry because the iterator has exactly one element. Therefore, the `NoSuchElementException` condition (no more elements) never occurs. The API documentation for `next` only declares `NoSuchElementException`. No other exceptions are mentioned, so only this one is relevant.
remark: The `next()` method throws `NoSuchElementException` when the iteration has no more elements. In this code, the iterator is obtained from the entry set of a singleton map, which always contains exactly one element. Thus, the iterator always has a next element, and calling `next()` will never trigger `NoSuchElementException`.
